A traditional Korean wedding (known as a *jorye* ) is `a rich cultural celebration rooted in Confucian values, balancing nature, family honor, and the joining of two households`.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXI0aQl2qvpRS3O3z7adaJrxq9jPnCfVwaTCYg_YWv8xvjJQV7BDVazsRxJnfFGrSsd84UAWKMG7bbwZMVTrWuriVa4g7eEdgco3Bbc9_-6jpg7JANdhDydAZmHfrVQMIO4Ge1BYsblfM0CxUi_Ocz_w)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXz46N2MQYfIy8aXI0lZTHTlNuuLavrLutre5ctmaF-c9iYWamsahp-6ZJa3UHN9kv_jXUpPQisojNSkysI59VGjwrYuwy_-CBoufA-iKRVAnxixqI5EA4x4OA9alODOu-mjNT-7TQX8PJWQ)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXP2YzqRNQkCEyOeHNASQCGXZYYY5quUNX4VmHRcWn3O0eRiva16jpErrfEsa8BK_8xvbk1ZFSkss0nEYCtq5RwaiYhgCBbpeFXxk29gZFcy7R0wYOvV_bUjKHo8C5Ohlj_X9V)

### Attire (Hanbok)

- **Bride:** Wears a colorful traditional [Hanbok](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtDZSf_HWGxRu4d13sovDR7IRrv_ztBE_FB6sJWK4iCLRINykIGCxjIx_FMOcYj8eg_Lznu_tkknM-pXa-ki0FBuENptgF8qJi9n7kdDteM9_YunBNQhe6ozheBbsziJxuC-vzuEc77aMJ7IXX4zwFjc) featuring a *chima* (full skirt) and *jeogori* (jacket), or an elaborate embroidered *wonsam* robe. Her face often bears small red dots (*yonji gongji* ) to ward off evil spirits.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtDZSf_HWGxRu4d13sovDR7IRrv_ztBE_FB6sJWK4iCLRINykIGCxjIx_FMOcYj8eg_Lznu_tkknM-pXa-ki0FBuENptgF8qJi9n7kdDteM9_YunBNQhe6ozheBbsziJxuC-vzuEc77aMJ7IXX4zwFjc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXP2YzqRNQkCEyOeHNASQCGXZYYY5quUNX4VmHRcWn3O0eRiva16jpErrfEsa8BK_8xvbk1ZFSkss0nEYCtq5RwaiYhgCBbpeFXxk29gZFcy7R0wYOvV_bUjKHo8C5Ohlj_X9V)
- **Groom:** Wears a Chosun-era official court outfit (*samogwandae* ) with wide trousers (*baji* ), a jacket (*jeogori* ), an elaborate belt, and a black cap with wings (*samo*).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtDZSf_HWGxRu4d13sovDR7IRrv_ztBE_FB6sJWK4iCLRINykIGCxjIx_FMOcYj8eg_Lznu_tkknM-pXa-ki0FBuENptgF8qJi9n7kdDteM9_YunBNQhe6ozheBbsziJxuC-vzuEc77aMJ7IXX4zwFjc)
- **Mothers:** The bride’s mother typically wears pink or purple, while the groom’s mother wears light blue or green.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtNwIHuo-zT6XE7tYJbyfTrJlT9fBdzcdIbw0hO3Nx7o5NINtA_yzrPqLA6TxLzSds6FWoK-y3EUyjnCOHqk4cSvSDkqSalgTUING5QUX-rbYPyAQ75SdZEA1jPO0fJJUA2WfOQFmKCcn4xyjiAZTEUg)

### Key Wedding Rituals (*Chorye*)

- **Processional & Candles:** The mothers of the bride and groom enter first, lighting red (bride) and blue (groom) candles to symbolize the balance of natural cosmic forces (*Yin and Yang*).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtDZSf_HWGxRu4d13sovDR7IRrv_ztBE_FB6sJWK4iCLRINykIGCxjIx_FMOcYj8eg_Lznu_tkknM-pXa-ki0FBuENptgF8qJi9n7kdDteM9_YunBNQhe6ozheBbsziJxuC-vzuEc77aMJ7IXX4zwFjc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXP2YzqRNQkCEyOeHNASQCGXZYYY5quUNX4VmHRcWn3O0eRiva16jpErrfEsa8BK_8xvbk1ZFSkss0nEYCtq5RwaiYhgCBbpeFXxk29gZFcy7R0wYOvV_bUjKHo8C5Ohlj_X9V)
- **Jeonan-rye (Wild Goose Gift):** Historically, the groom presented a wooden wild goose to the bride's family, symbolizing lifelong fidelity and loyalty, as geese mate for life.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbQHEIkXXlhkT5qysDmkMf9zMdTAscve-X9ldjaqCy4s4MwdFxtcFpa7UhruGKDnW-5QbUnTIN2xVW8gTABAqa6gjqBNQ6OEqmGcYfE-_NqR3I5XLj_Dnbd72bsDV3ZYu7OazVVM0zWbK2dFyFXc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXI0aQl2qvpRS3O3z7adaJrxq9jPnCfVwaTCYg_YWv8xvjJQV7BDVazsRxJnfFGrSsd84UAWKMG7bbwZMVTrWuriVa4g7eEdgco3Bbc9_-6jpg7JANdhDydAZmHfrVQMIO4Ge1BYsblfM0CxUi_Ocz_w)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtNwIHuo-zT6XE7tYJbyfTrJlT9fBdzcdIbw0hO3Nx7o5NINtA_yzrPqLA6TxLzSds6FWoK-y3EUyjnCOHqk4cSvSDkqSalgTUING5QUX-rbYPyAQ75SdZEA1jPO0fJJUA2WfOQFmKCcn4xyjiAZTEUg)
- **Gyo-bae-rye (Bowing Ritual):** The couple washes their hands to cleanse the past, then bows deeply to each other, to their parents, and to the heavens as witnesses.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXP2YzqRNQkCEyOeHNASQCGXZYYY5quUNX4VmHRcWn3O0eRiva16jpErrfEsa8BK_8xvbk1ZFSkss0nEYCtq5RwaiYhgCBbpeFXxk29gZFcy7R0wYOvV_bUjKHo8C5Ohlj_X9V)
- **Hap-geun-rye (Wine Sharing):** The couple drinks a special rice wine from two halves of a split gourd tied with a red and blue cord; once joined together, it symbolizes their union.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtNwIHuo-zT6XE7tYJbyfTrJlT9fBdzcdIbw0hO3Nx7o5NINtA_yzrPqLA6TxLzSds6FWoK-y3EUyjnCOHqk4cSvSDkqSalgTUING5QUX-rbYPyAQ75SdZEA1jPO0fJJUA2WfOQFmKCcn4xyjiAZTEUg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHEIkXXP2YzqRNQkCEyOeHNASQCGXZYYY5quUNX4VmHRcWn3O0eRiva16jpErrfEsa8BK_8xvbk1ZFSkss0nEYCtq5RwaiYhgCBbpeFXxk29gZFcy7R0wYOvV_bUjKHo8C5Ohlj_X9V)

### Post-Ceremony Tradition: The Pyebaek

- **Family Blessing:** Performed after the main ceremony in an intimate setting where the newlyweds pay respects to the groom's and bride's parents by making deep bows (*keunjeol* ) and serving rice wine or tea.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXwjZNjM3Rks1542z_QmtIXtwjYTyurl6BRu7yB073UhArBWtThh1iRewGcKDpJeZNq-LM0bCApqlEaZHZkYX-8WO5ajqpVPQtt_V5sfACin5foeHOfEr6uPPxQtdbcqzQQfSIhoIN_Q)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXI0aQl2qvpRS3O3z7adaJrxq9jPnCfVwaTCYg_YWv8xvjJQV7BDVazsRxJnfFGrSsd84UAWKMG7bbwZMVTrWuriVa4g7eEdgco3Bbc9_-6jpg7JANdhDydAZmHfrVQMIO4Ge1BYsblfM0CxUi_Ocz_w)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAES0AEBxCJF11W433KIdy5CFJ4J2WOZUxxUxEPvJrHb3xe5Ou0ExB_NbjCSb3FLS6a3-_LqNDS946Sr6soZ-my9EA8mSaDMopvAM-_d6zpdGG9aL3g4LG5CVzfU5VcDewz8sJ8jyLTE5CVaHz674cyRMD3KkfplzZm7GLFRetGL8liwngt28W5U_awtKnSmusxpiH1_ybiIBHmcf-k1asi22OHbwSY4hLqxBgOKufsidwVuljPlA1FKpZd2VXoqb3FYhk1-1odT8B5EixdzcNX7GSsZ)
- **Dates and Chestnuts:** Parents toss jujubes (dates) and chestnuts into a large cloth held by the couple; catching them represents how many children they will have (dates for sons, chestnuts for daughters).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShwEBxCJF19msNQ2yNDQjtScpQdzQyc1hf03ZGMMIHTckjZCLlnST5HE5bC_ncne22OmmV8WCrtXEkIUnl-5ElT__kMuz1CP7P7zRsyuCWe2WOYDh6uf4yQrDwSrqS-MGynHfCcYhBrdlEzaOAfCygL_kGINH70Hk-kYnx8QTLZ9lZqfoJSk6V1s)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXwjZNjM3Rks1542z_QmtIXtwjYTyurl6BRu7yB073UhArBWtThh1iRewGcKDpJeZNq-LM0bCApqlEaZHZkYX-8WO5ajqpVPQtt_V5sfACin5foeHOfEr6uPPxQtdbcqzQQfSIhoIN_Q)
- **Piggyback Ride:** The ceremony often ends with the groom piggybacking the bride in a circle as a symbol of strength and care.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXwjZNjM3Rks1542z_QmtIXtwjYTyurl6BRu7yB073UhArBWtThh1iRewGcKDpJeZNq-LM0bCApqlEaZHZkYX-8WO5ajqpVPQtt_V5sfACin5foeHOfEr6uPPxQtdbcqzQQfSIhoIN_Q)

### Modern Korean Weddings
Many couples today opt for a fusion approach: a quick 25-to-30-minute Western-style ceremony in a commercial wedding hall, followed by a large buffet for guests, and a separate, condensed *Pyebaek* room session in traditional attire for close family.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbwHEIkXXz46N2MQYfIy8aXI0lZTHTlNuuLavrLutre5ctmaF-c9iYWamsahp-6ZJa3UHN9kv_jXUpPQisojNSkysI59VGjwrYuwy_-CBoufA-iKRVAnxixqI5EA4x4OA9alODOu-mjNT-7TQX8PJWQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtDZSf_HWGxRu4d13sovDR7IRrv_ztBE_FB6sJWK4iCLRINykIGCxjIx_FMOcYj8eg_Lznu_tkknM-pXa-ki0FBuENptgF8qJi9n7kdDteM9_YunBNQhe6ozheBbsziJxuC-vzuEc77aMJ7IXX4zwFjc)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXtNwIHuo-zT6XE7tYJbyfTrJlT9fBdzcdIbw0hO3Nx7o5NINtA_yzrPqLA6TxLzSds6FWoK-y3EUyjnCOHqk4cSvSDkqSalgTUING5QUX-rbYPyAQ75SdZEA1jPO0fJJUA2WfOQFmKCcn4xyjiAZTEUg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHEIkXXI0aQl2qvpRS3O3z7adaJrxq9jPnCfVwaTCYg_YWv8xvjJQV7BDVazsRxJnfFGrSsd84UAWKMG7bbwZMVTrWuriVa4g7eEdgco3Bbc9_-6jpg7JANdhDydAZmHfrVQMIO4Ge1BYsblfM0CxUi_Ocz_w)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgwEBxCJF10nDNhSOIIY_f5kCG1iIvmCqxPcNq-H0khrSvpx252JscGPhJuIsq6gilJExtj-lBpHM6nA-CtbRLbNlkJxZCh_TYWeh5Q-5LULF_YxUs4bkRjdCNECQeSMRWSd7dlBWQYT5vGinPTkr5QqDDgEEo09oMxaHZgz6juaWklYgWQ)If you are planning an event or looking into specific customs, let me know:
